I want to confirm by checking the middleware package's `agents()` API to understand how the delegation list controls which agents triage can route to, and verify the refundAgent's interrupt/store setup isn't itself the problem before concluding the fix is just adding refundAgent back to the list.

I've confirmed delegation tools only get generated for agents listed in config.agents, so triage can't reach refundAgent without adding it there, and the system prompt's sub-agents list should follow the same config. Now I'm also wondering whether the refund sub-agent's use of interrupts, which relies on its store, could cause issues when delegated to through the agents middleware.

Since refundAgent has a store it's server-managed, like triage, while orderAgent lacking a store is client-managed — only client-managed agents can accept ad-hoc seeding, per the comment around line 346. I want to check lines 330-360 to make sure seeding historyLength into the store-backed refundAgent won't throw an error, since that would mean my fix is incomplete.

Confirmed: delegation tools are generated only for names in `config.agents`, so triage cannot reach `refundAgent`. Before editing, I'll check the history-seeding branch at line ~346, since `refundAgent` has a store and `historyLength` is set.

Good, the server-managed sub-agent case is handled gracefully, so now I'll fix line 55 in agents.ts. The refundAgent interrupt scenario is beyond scope here since the actual bug report is about missing approval requests; I'll make the fix and verify with a type-check rather than actually running genkit start.

I'll update the agents list to include both 'orderAgent' and 'refundAgent' in the agents() configuration call, keeping maxDelegations and historyLength unchanged.
History forwarding is skipped for server-managed sub-agents, so adding `refundAgent` to the delegation list won't throw. Making the one-line fix now.

text: Type checking passes, so I'll write the answer.json now. The key evidence is that the triage agent's middleware only registers delegation tools for names explicitly listed in its config, so it has no delegate_to_refundAgent tool while the orderAgent route works fine—I should note in the evidence that I verified this through code inspection rather than an end-to-end run.

The root cause is in the triage agent's delegation list: `src/agents.ts` line 55 only allows delegation to `orderAgent`, so refund requests have no route to `refundAgent`. I changed it to `agents({ agents: ['orderAgent', 'refundAgent'], maxDelegations: 3, historyLength: 4 })`. `answer.json` is written at the project root, and `tsc --noEmit` passes.

I did not run the flow end to end against the model, so the refund approval path is confirmed by code reading, not by a live run. The middleware only builds delegation tools for names in `config.agents`, which is why order questions still work and refunds don't.
